Hon'Ble
Shri Justice Pavan Kumar Dwivedi

On The 27th Of September, 2025
 Misc. Appeal No. 626 of 2014
 Sohan
 Versus
 Jitendra And Others
 Appearance:
 Ms. Pooja Nikam - Advocate for the appellant.

Shri Dilkush Kumawat - Advocate appearing on behalf o
 Saxena - Advocate for respondent No.2.

Order 
1. With consent of learned counsel for the parties the matter is finally heard.

2. This appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been preferred by the appellant / claimant being aggrieved by the award dated 14.2.2014 passed in MACC No.80/2011 by the Member, Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Indore whereby a total sum of Rs.19,676/- has been awarded to the appellant / claimant by way of compensation.
The challenge is to the quantum of compensation.

3. Short facts of the case are that on 28.3.2009, when the appellant was going for his work and as soon as he reached Gram Karlai, in front of Sugar Mill, Sanver Kshipra Road, at that time the offending vehicle (tractor) bearing registration No. M.P. 11/A-8804 driven by respondent No.1 came NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:28699 2 MA-626-2014 rashly and negligently and dashed the appellant due to which the appellant suffered grievous injuries.
He was admitted in the hospital from 28.3.2009 to 31.3.2009.
4. The claims tribunal after considering the evidence available on record awarded a total compensation of Rs.19,676/- to the appellant.
5. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that it has been duly proved before the tribunal that the appellant has suffered injuries due to the rash and negligent driving of the insured vehicle.
He had remained under treatment for which Exhibits P/24 to P/47 were produced before the claims tribunal in which the appellant proved that he has suffered head injury.

He remained hospitalized Sohan vs Jitendra on 27 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/6988697/
1 for a period from 28.3.2009 to 31.3.2009 underwent C.T. Scan report for which is Exhibited as P/6 and MLC was done which is Exhibit P/5.
As such she submits that for all these treatments and injuries the meager amount of Rs.90,000/- has been awarded by the claims tribunal which is inadequate and not just compensation.
6. Per contra, learned counsel for the Insurance Co. submits that looking to the simple nature of injuries the amount of compensation is just and proper hence prays for dismissal of the appeal.

7. Heard the learned counsel for the parties, perused the record.
8.
From perusal of the record, it is seen that the injuries were simple in nature.
However, there was one injury on head for which appellant remained hospitalized for a period of 3 days.
The appellant also underwent C.T. Scan which shows that the appellant has suffered the injuries due to rash and negligent driving of the insured vehicle.

As such in the considering view of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:28699 3 MA-626-2014 this Court it will constituted just compensation if another amount of Rs.25,000/- is awarded over and above the amount already awarded by the claims tribunal.

Hence the appeal is disposed off by awarding an amount of Rs.25,000/- in addition to the amount already awarded by the claims tribunal which shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of application before the claims tribunal.

However the period from 22.4.2015 on which date the appeal was dismissed for non-compliance of common conditional order and restored on 9/9/2017, shall not be taken into consideration for calculation of interest on the awarded amount.
9. Accordingly, the appeal is allowed in part and disposed off.

(PAVAN KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE SS/-
